records.c: The 48 bytes beyond the high-RAM copy limit match record 306 byte for byte starting at its offset $800. They remain in the staging buffer after $6232 completes the copy.
First 64-byte sprite slot in the copy. Rendering its first 63 bytes shows a small foot shape at the lower left.
Upright body shape in the second slot, beside the first foot and narrow contour slots.
Narrow curved shape to the right of the body in the third sprite slot.
Small lower-left shape in the first slot of the second three-slot group.
Upright torso and leg silhouette in the middle slot of the second group.
Curved right-side silhouette matching the second group of body and foot slots.
Small lower-left shape in the first slot of the third group.
Upright body shape with a more extended arm in the third group.
Narrow side shape paired with the last upright body.

First destination plane of the three-plane sprite builder. The AND-and-store path at $635F and the replacement path at $6388 write this slot. The copy at $63CA fills it from the agent sprites using the original VIC pointers.
Second 64-byte plane used by the builder. The writes at $636B and $638B parallel the updates to the first plane.
Third 64-byte plane used by the builder. The writes at $6374 and $638E use the same row index.
All 63 visible sprite bytes are zero. The trailing stride byte is $04.

Record 315 offsets $340–$37F. Fifteen four-byte groups begin with $04 $00 and the last begins with $04 $80. The third byte is normally $FF, except $7E at $F75E and $7F at $F77E. VICE wrote the first byte at $622B, completing the backward copy of these three slots.
Record 315 offsets $380–$3BF. Four-byte groups repeat $00 $04 $FB $FF, with $85 at $F785 and $16 at $F7BF. The latter falls on the stride byte of the second 64-byte slot.

Record 315 offsets $3C0–$3FF. This slot repeats $00 $04 $FB $FF, except $84 at $F7FD. The bytes through $F7FF are part of the near-identical stretch at record 267 offsets $1F90–$1FFF, which begins within the preceding slot.
Sprite-sized shape immediately before the similar shape at $F840 and the speech driver. The image has a rounded striped top over a wide base.
Second rounded striped shape. The speech driver's first NMI instruction begins at the next slot boundary.

Save A, read a value from the patched wave pointer in page four, halve it into SID volume and acknowledge CIA2. Increment the low operand and count down $8A. At zero switch to $F8A1 and pass it the last low operand.

Output the same half-amplitude from the backward wave pointer and decrement its low operand until $8B reaches zero. Continue to the shared state advance when $8D is zero or select the constant-volume NMI otherwise.
Output volume seven, acknowledge CIA2 and decrement the quiet-interval counter $8D. If it remains nonzero, install $F8D4 as a shorter interrupt that leaves the volume alone.
Acknowledge CIA2 and count the remaining quiet ticks in $8D. When it expires, continue at $F8EC, where A is saved for the shared tail.
Stop CIA2 timer B with $90, restore volume seven and acknowledge the pending CIA2 interrupt before returning.
Save A on entry from the quiet-tick interrupt, then enter the shared state advance.

Install the next low NMI vector byte from $8E, load the next wave offset and reset the forward, backward and quiet counters. Increment $94 and follow the segment path or the interval path selected by the patched jump.
Save X and Y, increment $92 and read a descriptor when it wraps. Reload $94 from $93, toggle bit six of the old waveform offset to form X and call through the operand patched at $F920.
Restore Y, X and A in reverse push order before returning from the NMI.
Save X and Y, rebuild the alternate wave when $97 differs from $8F and advance the timing stream. Rejoin the shared register restore at $F922.
Set $8E to $DC so the next state advance installs the timer-stopping handler.
Set the next NMI low byte to $C0 and initialize the quiet duration field $91 to $80.
Tail-call $FA58 to set the initial waveform offset in $8F before rebuilding the buffer.

Decode packed levels through $F9D6, then inspect bit six of the descriptor byte patched into $F969. One branch toggles that bit and selects the just-decoded wave, while the other mixes waves before advancing the timing stream.

Test the descriptor state patched into $F969. A negative value reinstalls the stop call. Otherwise read the descriptor at $84, load its counters, optionally build the source pointer from the base at $FAFA and patch the interval jump and waveform dispatch.
Four waveform lengths indexed by two bits rotated out of the segment descriptor. The selected byte is written to $90.
Advance the descriptor pointer $84/$85 by four bytes, carrying into the high byte.

Add the selected wave length to the caller-supplied offset in A and patch the exit comparison. Decode pairs of five-bit even volume values from ($88), writing them to page four and advancing the source pointer as each packed byte is consumed.

Increment the repeat counter. While it is nonzero, add the signed byte at $9A to the timing level and halve the result into $91. At rollover, read two new bytes from ($86), rebuild the counter and take the next increment from $FA48.
Sixteen timing increments selected by the low nibble of the second timing byte. $FA13 adds the selected byte to $99 on subsequent intervals.
Store the accumulator in $8F before falling through to the buffer mixer.
Patch two source offsets into page four and choose the opposite output half. Average the source values with ADC and ROR for $90 entries, then store the output offset in $8F.
Initialize the descriptor and timing pointers, stop timer B, install the NMI vector in page $F8, set its first phase and restart the timer. The resident JSR at $3609 reached this entry in VICE.
Return bit zero of CIA2 timer B control in A. The resident poll shifts that bit into carry.
Write $90 to timer B control and branch to the shared status read.
Write $91 to timer B control, program latch $0064, enable timer B interrupts through $DD0D and acknowledge the pending flags.
Patch the shared state advance to use its first interval target and stop callback. Set its counters to $FE, install the constant-volume NMI and give it a one-tick initial duration.
Read the base at $FAFA into $84/$85 and use base plus eight for the timing pointer at $86/$87. Set the repeat counter to $FF and clear the mutable descriptor byte at $F969.
Little-endian base pointer used by the speech decoder. It holds $0740 in the loaded record.
Start the speech driver, poll timer B's running bit through $FA98 and return once it clears.

A zero byte followed by a 16-bit x86 fragment. Its two relative CALLs at $FB08 and $FB32 have the same destination. Each tests AX after the call, and both conditional paths can reach the BP-relative load at $FB3D. The cassette copy places these bytes after the 6510 speech routine and before the next sprite slot.
A rounded striped silhouette occupies the drawable bytes of this slot, with single-byte stride padding before the next graphic.
Three nonzero rows of multicolour pixels in the first three bytes of their respective rows, followed by blank rows.
Small centered round shape in the sprite slot before the taller striped shapes at $FC00.
Striped body with tapered central shaft, rendered from 21 three-byte rows.
Taller striped shaft and a base in the following 64-byte slot.
Wide silhouette with an angled upper section. The next image preserves its base while changing the upper pixels.
Second wide silhouette in the copied record. The engine uses this address as writable sprite storage after startup.
Bright rounded shape with a pedestal in the original copy, before the engine overwrites this region.
A second upright pedestal frame with shifted stripe pixels, from the same copied group.
Large diagonal hand-shaped silhouette in the original copy. The later elevator snapshot differs across this slot.
Thin horizontal shape with an enlarged left end.
Orange angular silhouette in the top half of its 21-row cell.
Horizontal striped shape with a sloping upper edge.
Thin bright bar near the center of its cell with solid ends.
Rectangular display with a lighter rim and rows of pixels beneath.
Low profile with a stepped left edge and a taller column at right.
Two narrow upright shapes joined by a short bridge at the top.
First rectangular panel with alternating interior stripes. It still matches the cassette data in the opening elevator.
Second rectangular panel in the last copied sprite slot. Subsequent engine writes reuse this slot for actor fields and hardware vectors.
